procedures.title: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy
procedures.summary: Remove the gallbladder after establishing the critical view of safety: clear the hepatocystic triangle until only the cystic duct and cystic artery enter the gallbladder, then clip, divide, and dissect it off the liver bed.

hints: The camera goes in first so every other port is placed under direct vision.
steps.title: Open umbilical access
steps.instruction: Enter the peritoneum at the umbilicus with an open technique, place the 12 mm camera port, and insufflate.

mistakes.feedback: The trocar tip contacted the liver. Watch each trocar enter under the camera.

hints: Spread the ports so instruments triangulate on the gallbladder instead of clashing.
steps.title: Place working ports
steps.instruction: Under vision, place the epigastric port and two right subcostal 5 mm ports.

hints: Cephalad fundus retraction lifts the liver edge and exposes the gallbladder neck.
steps.title: Retract the fundus
steps.instruction: Grasp the gallbladder fundus through the lateral port and push it cephalad over the liver.

mistakes.feedback: Medial traction aligns the cystic duct with the common bile duct, the classic setup for misidentification. Pull lateral.

hints: Lateral traction widens the angle between the cystic duct and the common bile duct.
steps.title: Retract the infundibulum laterally
steps.instruction: Grasp the infundibulum and pull laterally and inferiorly to open the hepatocystic triangle.

mistakes.feedback: Energy touched the common bile duct. Stay on the gallbladder side, high on the neck.
Energy touched the right hepatic artery. It can loop close to the triangle.

hints: Dissect close to the gallbladder, both anterior and posterior, before naming any structure.
steps.title: Clear the hepatocystic triangle
steps.instruction: Open the peritoneum on both sides of the gallbladder neck and clear fat and fibrous tissue from the triangle.

mistakes.feedback: That is the common bile duct. Clipping it here is the classic bile duct injury. Return to dissection.
That is the common hepatic duct, not the cystic duct.

hints: Two and only two structures should enter the gallbladder. If you cannot see that, keep dissecting or bail out.
steps.title: Confirm the critical view of safety
steps.instruction: Name the two structures entering the gallbladder. Only the cystic duct and cystic artery should remain, with the lower gallbladder lifted off the liver.

mistakes.feedback: That clip caught the right hepatic artery.

steps.title: Clip the cystic artery
steps.instruction: Apply clips to the cystic artery: two on the patient side, one on the gallbladder side.

mistakes.feedback: That clip is on the common bile duct.

hints: Clips should cross the full width of the duct without catching surrounding tissue.
steps.title: Clip the cystic duct
steps.instruction: Apply clips to the cystic duct: two on the patient side, one on the gallbladder side.

hints: Leave two clips on the patient side of every cut.
steps.title: Divide the duct and artery
steps.instruction: Cut the cystic artery and cystic duct between the clips with scissors.

mistakes.feedback: You entered the liver bed. Too deep bleeds; too shallow perforates the gallbladder.

steps.title: Dissect off the liver bed
steps.instruction: Separate the gallbladder from the cystic plate with the hook, staying in the plane against the gallbladder wall.

steps.title: Check hemostasis
steps.instruction: Inspect the liver bed and clips, irrigate, and suction until clear.

steps.title: Extract the gallbladder
steps.instruction: Place the gallbladder in a retrieval bag and remove it through the umbilical port.

steps.title: Close
steps.instruction: Remove ports under vision, release the pneumoperitoneum, and close the fascia at the 12 mm sites.

procedures.title: Laparoscopic appendectomy
procedures.summary: Find the appendix by following the taeniae of the cecum, divide the mesoappendix with its artery, secure and divide the appendix base, and remove it in a bag.

steps.title: Open umbilical access
steps.instruction: Enter at the umbilicus with an open technique, place the camera port, and insufflate.

mistakes.feedback: The suprapubic trocar hit the bladder. It should be emptied before surgery and the trocar watched in.

steps.title: Place working ports
steps.instruction: Place the left lower quadrant and suprapubic ports under vision.

mistakes.feedback: Grasping an inflamed appendix can perforate it. Hold the mesoappendix instead.

hints: All three taeniae converge on the appendix base.
steps.title: Locate the appendix
steps.instruction: Tilt head down and left side down, sweep the small bowel away, and follow the taeniae of the cecum to the appendix base.

steps.title: Assess the appendix
steps.instruction: Look for perforation, abscess, or a mass, and run the terminal ileum.

steps.title: Window the mesoappendix
steps.instruction: Create a window in the mesoappendix right at the appendix base.

mistakes.feedback: The sealer jaws were on the terminal ileum. Thermal spread can cause a delayed leak.

steps.title: Divide the mesoappendix
steps.instruction: Seal and divide the mesoappendix, including the appendicular artery.

mistakes.feedback: Too much cecum in the jaws. Stay at the base.
The stapler caught the terminal ileum.

hints: A long stump left behind can cause stump appendicitis later.
steps.title: Staple the appendix base
steps.instruction: Fire the stapler across the appendix flush with the cecum.

steps.title: Extract the appendix
steps.instruction: Bag the appendix and remove it through the umbilical port without touching the wound.

steps.title: Suction and inspect
steps.instruction: Suction any fluid from the right lower quadrant and pelvis and check the staple line.

steps.title: Close
steps.instruction: Remove ports under vision, release the pneumoperitoneum, and close the umbilical fascia.

procedures.title: Laparoscopic sigmoid colectomy
procedures.summary: Resect the diseased sigmoid colon: identify and protect the left ureter, divide the inferior mesenteric vessels, mobilize the colon, transect the upper rectum, and restore continuity with a stapled colorectal anastomosis.

steps.title: Open umbilical access
steps.instruction: Enter at the umbilicus with an open technique, place the camera port, and insufflate.

steps.title: Place working ports
steps.instruction: Place the right lower, right upper, and left lower quadrant ports under vision.

steps.title: Clear the operative field
steps.instruction: Head down, right side down. Sweep the omentum above the transverse colon and the small bowel out of the pelvis.

steps.title: Score the sigmoid mesentery
steps.instruction: Lift the sigmoid mesocolon and score the peritoneum at the sacral promontory beneath the inferior mesenteric artery.

mistakes.feedback: Those are the gonadal vessels. The ureter lies deeper and peristalses when touched.

hints: The ureter crosses the iliac vessels near their bifurcation.
steps.title: Identify the left ureter
steps.instruction: Dissect medial to lateral under the mesentery and positively identify the left ureter and gonadal vessels before dividing anything.

mistakes.feedback: The ureter was in the sealer jaws.

steps.title: Divide the inferior mesenteric artery
steps.instruction: With the ureter safe, seal and divide the inferior mesenteric artery.

steps.title: Mobilize the colon laterally
steps.instruction: Release the lateral attachments of the sigmoid and descending colon along the white line of Toldt.

hints: Leaving sigmoid behind raises recurrence risk. Transect on soft rectum where the taeniae splay.
steps.title: Transect the upper rectum
steps.instruction: Fire the linear stapler across the upper rectum below the diseased segment.

steps.title: Extract and divide proximally
steps.instruction: Bring the specimen out through a protected small incision, divide the proximal colon, and seat the stapler anvil.

mistakes.feedback: Pelvic tissue was caught in the stapler.

steps.title: Create the anastomosis
steps.instruction: Pass the circular stapler transanally and join the descending colon to the rectum, with no tension and no twist.

steps.title: Leak test
steps.instruction: Fill the pelvis with saline, clamp above the anastomosis, and insufflate the rectum. No bubbles means no leak.

steps.title: Close
steps.instruction: Remove ports under vision, release the pneumoperitoneum, and close the extraction site and 12 mm fascia.

flags.title: Bleeding risk: anticoagulant plus antiplatelet
flags.spoken: bleeding risk from apixaban and aspirin
flags.detail: Active apixaban and aspirin. Combined anticoagulant and antiplatelet therapy compounds bleeding risk. The hold and restart plan must be confirmed with the care team before incision.

flags.title: Allergy: Sulfonamide (high severity)
flags.spoken: a high severity allergy to Sulfonamide
flags.detail: Allergies on file: Sulfonamide. Prophylactic antibiotics and perioperative drugs must be chosen around them.

flags.title: Metformin with eGFR below 45
flags.detail: Metformin is active while eGFR is 31. Lactic acidosis risk rises around surgery and contrast; the hold plan needs confirming.

flags.title: Cardiac: Atrial fibrillation, Heart failure
flags.detail: Pneumoperitoneum and positioning change venous return and afterload. Anesthesia needs to know before insufflation.

flags.title: Contrast media allergy
flags.detail: Contrast allergy on file. Any cholangiogram, CT, or contrast study needs an allergy plan first.

flags.title: Reduced kidney function (eGFR 31)
flags.spoken: reduced kidney function with an e G F R of 31
flags.detail: Renally cleared drugs, contrast, and prolonged high-pressure pneumoperitoneum all need adjustment.

flags.title: Diabetes (A1c 6.8%)
flags.spoken: diabetes with an A one C of 6.8
flags.detail: Perioperative glucose monitoring needed. Glucose-lowering drugs: metformin hydrochloride 500 MG Oral Tablet.

flags.title: Anemia (hemoglobin 11.4)
flags.detail: Lower tolerance for blood loss. Type and screen, and know the latest hemoglobin before incision.

flags.title: Polypharmacy (14 active medications)
flags.detail: Medication reconciliation is required: which to continue, hold, or restart after surgery.

brief.say: Harriet Lindqvist, 78. Four high priority: bleeding risk from apixaban and aspirin, a high severity allergy to Sulfonamide, metformin with low kidney function, and atrial fibrillation with heart failure. Also a contrast allergy, reduced kidney function with an e G F R of 31, diabetes with an A one C of 6.8, anemia with a hemoglobin of 11.4, 14 active medications, and age 78. Synthetic demo patient.
brief.disclaimer: Synthetic FinchNode demo data. Flags and cases are illustrative teaching material, not clinical guidance.

considerations.note: Anticoagulant or antiplatelet on board: this is the step most likely to bleed. Confirm the documented hold before incision and seal precisely.
Bleeding risk patient: inspect every raw surface and clip line twice before leaving.
Allergy on file: confirm the prophylactic antibiotic was chosen around it before incision.
Metformin with low eGFR: confirm it was held. Watch for acidosis if the case runs long.
Cardiac disease: insufflate slowly and warn anesthesia. Pneumoperitoneum and tilt change venous return.
Contrast allergy: an intraoperative contrast study needs an allergy plan. Rely on clear anatomic identification.
Reduced kidney function: high-pressure pneumoperitoneum lowers renal blood flow. Use the lowest pressure that gives a working view.
Diabetes: glucose checked before incision and monitored through the case.
Preoperative anemia: little reserve for blood loss. Know the latest hemoglobin and whether blood is available.
Many active medications: the reconciliation list should be on the board before the time out.
Older adult: lower reserve. Keep the case efficient and watch temperature and fluids.

procedure.title: Laparoscopic sigmoid colectomy
procedure.summary: Resect the diseased sigmoid colon: identify and protect the left ureter, divide the inferior mesenteric vessels, mobilize the colon, transect the upper rectum, and restore continuity with a stapled colorectal anastomosis.

steps.title: Open umbilical access
steps.instruction: Enter at the umbilicus with an open technique, place the camera port, and insufflate.

steps.title: Place working ports
steps.instruction: Place the right lower, right upper, and left lower quadrant ports under vision.

steps.title: Clear the operative field
steps.instruction: Head down, right side down. Sweep the omentum above the transverse colon and the small bowel out of the pelvis.

steps.title: Score the sigmoid mesentery
steps.instruction: Lift the sigmoid mesocolon and score the peritoneum at the sacral promontory beneath the inferior mesenteric artery.

mistakes.feedback: Those are the gonadal vessels. The ureter lies deeper and peristalses when touched.

hints: The ureter crosses the iliac vessels near their bifurcation.
steps.title: Identify the left ureter
steps.instruction: Dissect medial to lateral under the mesentery and positively identify the left ureter and gonadal vessels before dividing anything.

mistakes.feedback: The ureter was in the sealer jaws.

steps.title: Divide the inferior mesenteric artery
steps.instruction: With the ureter safe, seal and divide the inferior mesenteric artery.

steps.title: Mobilize the colon laterally
steps.instruction: Release the lateral attachments of the sigmoid and descending colon along the white line of Toldt.

hints: Leaving sigmoid behind raises recurrence risk. Transect on soft rectum where the taeniae splay.
steps.title: Transect the upper rectum
steps.instruction: Fire the linear stapler across the upper rectum below the diseased segment.

steps.title: Extract and divide proximally
steps.instruction: Bring the specimen out through a protected small incision, divide the proximal colon, and seat the stapler anvil.

mistakes.feedback: Pelvic tissue was caught in the stapler.

steps.title: Create the anastomosis
steps.instruction: Pass the circular stapler transanally and join the descending colon to the rectum, with no tension and no twist.

steps.title: Leak test
steps.instruction: Fill the pelvis with saline, clamp above the anastomosis, and insufflate the rectum. No bubbles means no leak.

steps.title: Close
steps.instruction: Remove ports under vision, release the pneumoperitoneum, and close the extraction site and 12 mm fascia.

procedure.title: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy
procedure.summary: Remove the gallbladder after establishing the critical view of safety: clear the hepatocystic triangle until only the cystic duct and cystic artery enter the gallbladder, then clip, divide, and dissect it off the liver bed.

hints: The camera goes in first so every other port is placed under direct vision.
steps.title: Open umbilical access
steps.instruction: Enter the peritoneum at the umbilicus with an open technique, place the 12 mm camera port, and insufflate.

mistakes.feedback: The trocar tip contacted the liver. Watch each trocar enter under the camera.

hints: Spread the ports so instruments triangulate on the gallbladder instead of clashing.
steps.title: Place working ports
steps.instruction: Under vision, place the epigastric port and two right subcostal 5 mm ports.

hints: Cephalad fundus retraction lifts the liver edge and exposes the gallbladder neck.
steps.title: Retract the fundus
steps.instruction: Grasp the gallbladder fundus through the lateral port and push it cephalad over the liver.

mistakes.feedback: Medial traction aligns the cystic duct with the common bile duct, the classic setup for misidentification. Pull lateral.

hints: Lateral traction widens the angle between the cystic duct and the common bile duct.
steps.title: Retract the infundibulum laterally
steps.instruction: Grasp the infundibulum and pull laterally and inferiorly to open the hepatocystic triangle.

mistakes.feedback: Energy touched the common bile duct. Stay on the gallbladder side, high on the neck.
Energy touched the right hepatic artery. It can loop close to the triangle.

hints: Dissect close to the gallbladder, both anterior and posterior, before naming any structure.
steps.title: Clear the hepatocystic triangle
steps.instruction: Open the peritoneum on both sides of the gallbladder neck and clear fat and fibrous tissue from the triangle.

mistakes.feedback: That is the common bile duct. Clipping it here is the classic bile duct injury. Return to dissection.
That is the common hepatic duct, not the cystic duct.

hints: Two and only two structures should enter the gallbladder. If you cannot see that, keep dissecting or bail out.
steps.title: Confirm the critical view of safety
steps.instruction: Name the two structures entering the gallbladder. Only the cystic duct and cystic artery should remain, with the lower gallbladder lifted off the liver.

mistakes.feedback: That clip caught the right hepatic artery.

steps.title: Clip the cystic artery
steps.instruction: Apply clips to the cystic artery: two on the patient side, one on the gallbladder side.

mistakes.feedback: That clip is on the common bile duct.

hints: Clips should cross the full width of the duct without catching surrounding tissue.
steps.title: Clip the cystic duct
steps.instruction: Apply clips to the cystic duct: two on the patient side, one on the gallbladder side.

hints: Leave two clips on the patient side of every cut.
steps.title: Divide the duct and artery
steps.instruction: Cut the cystic artery and cystic duct between the clips with scissors.

mistakes.feedback: You entered the liver bed. Too deep bleeds; too shallow perforates the gallbladder.

steps.title: Dissect off the liver bed
steps.instruction: Separate the gallbladder from the cystic plate with the hook, staying in the plane against the gallbladder wall.

steps.title: Check hemostasis
steps.instruction: Inspect the liver bed and clips, irrigate, and suction until clear.

steps.title: Extract the gallbladder
steps.instruction: Place the gallbladder in a retrieval bag and remove it through the umbilical port.

steps.title: Close
steps.instruction: Remove ports under vision, release the pneumoperitoneum, and close the fascia at the 12 mm sites.
